content.text:
I couldn't open any files, so this diagnosis comes from the bug report and the usual structure of this boilerplate. I haven't confirmed it against the actual code.

The symptoms point to the wrong ID being excluded when other sessions are deleted after a password change. The "sometimes survives" detail fits an exclusion keyed on the user ID rather than the session ID. A session that happens to share that numeric ID would then be spared by coincidence, while the caller's real session is deleted.

The likely place is `AuthService.update`. It probably calls `sessionService.deleteByUserIdWithExclude` with `excludeId: userJwtPayload.id` (the user ID) instead of `userJwtPayload.sessionId`. The line numbers below are estimates.

The session repositories are weaker candidates. Their exclude filter could be inverted or mistyped, for example a bad `Not(...)` comparison or `$not`/`$ne` handling in the Mongo version.

candidates.explanation: After a password change, the call to sessionService.deleteByUserIdWithExclude most likely passes the wrong value as excludeId, such as the user id (userJwtPayload.id) instead of the current session id (userJwtPayload.sessionId). The caller's own session is then not excluded and gets deleted, so its next refresh returns 401. A different session whose id equals the user id is spared by coincidence, which explains why an older session sometimes survives.
The exclusion filter used to delete the user's other sessions may be wrong. For example, the Not(excludeId) condition may be mistyped or mis-cast, so the current session is not protected.

The Mongo variant has the same risk: the $not/$ne exclusion on _id may not match because of an ObjectId vs string mismatch or an incorrect operator, so the current session is deleted along with the others.

fix.description: In AuthService.update, when the password changes, call sessionService.deleteByUserIdWithExclude({ userId: currentUser.id, excludeId: userJwtPayload.sessionId }). Pass the session id from the JWT payload, not the user id. Also check that the repository exclusion filters compare against the session id with the correct type.
